checks.item: 4. Line endings: do fresh worktrees fail hash checks?
checks.evidence: core.autocrlf=true (system gitconfig), no .gitattributes. Blobs are LF everywhere (git ls-files --eol: i/lf). Every hash is over raw bytes: records.py split_hash uses read_bytes; check_splits.py uses f.read_bytes(). The older manifests were computed over CRLF working-tree bytes: datasets/splits/scenarios.json dev hash bc875601... equals sha256 of the CRLF checkout of datasets/scenarios/dev.jsonl, whereas the LF blob hashes abceafb6.... The new manifest datasets/splits/scenarios-extra.json holds a hash of LF bytes (27febb46..., equal to the blob hash). Fresh-checkout evidence: I cloned with --no-checkout into the scratchpad and checked out e130a28 under autocrlf=true: scenarios dev and test hashes match their manifests (CRLF), but scenarios_extra dev.jsonl is CRLF and does NOT match (False). This worktree's scenarios_extra files are w/lf only because the builder rechecked them out plain. Details are in notes; classified as a real bug in build's extra-cases commit, but not in T4.2's code or results. Per instruction I did not fix it.

notes: 1. REAL BUG, outside T4.2's code and results, for the coordinator to fix on build: datasets/splits/scenarios-extra.json hashes LF bytes while every earlier manifest (scenarios, and records' dataset_hash via split_hash) hashes the CRLF bytes that autocrlf=true produces on this Windows machine. In any fresh worktree or clone made here, scenarios_extra/dev.jsonl is CRLF, so tests/test_extra_cases.py line 125 (check_splits has no scenarios-extra problem) and any load_verified('scenarios_extra', ...) fail, as would a future record built on it (none exists yet). The reverse holds on a Linux or LF checkout: all the older manifests would fail. This worktree passes only because the builder rechecked the extra files out as LF. The cleanest fix is a .gitattributes with '* text eol=lf' (or '-text' on datasets/ and results/) plus recomputing the older manifests and record hashes, or hashing with CRLF normalised; either needs care because records already store CRLF-based hashes. Since the gate's acceptance commands (test_e3, check_run E3) use only the older sources, they pass in a fresh worktree and this bug does not affect them. 2. Lesser gap: rebuild_records cannot re-derive pre-merge records because of the new null field (see check 3c). 3. check_run E2 took over two minutes in this environment, so the gate log's 41 s for test_e3 is the only timing recorded. 4. The gate log carries only E3 check_run; I ran E2 myself and it passed.
